question: What aspects can be studied using a coupled system of qubits and mechanical resonators?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer must identify transduction of superconducting qubit excitations to optical photons as a studyable aspect, with the mechanical mode acting as intermediary.
examples: A mechanical mode mediates transduction between a qubit and an optical mode
The coupled system converts a superconducting qubit excitation into an optical photon

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer must describe the architecture of a qubit, mechanical resonator, and optical mode, with the qubit coupled to mechanics via a resonant piezoelectric interaction and mechanics to optics via a parametric optomechanical interaction.
examples: Piezoelectric coupling (rate gpe) links the qubit and mechanical mode
The mechanical mode couples to an optical mode via a parametric optomechanical interaction

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer must identify quantum erasure using surface acoustic wave phonons as an application, exploiting a two-phonon entangled state where the herald phonon marks which-path information and slow phonon propagation delays detection until after the interferometric result.
examples: A two-phonon entangled state with the second phonon marking which-path information
Slow SAW propagation allows which-path detection after the interferogram is recorded

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer must mention that improved transduction paves the way for system-level demonstrations of remote entanglement of superconducting qubits and acoustic quantum state transfer in quantum networks.
examples: Improved transduction efficiency enables system-level remote entanglement demonstrations
High-fidelity acoustic quantum state transfer in a quantum network

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer must mention that the quantum eraser builds on a previously demonstrated SAW-based interferometer whose interferogram is observed.
examples: Building on a previously demonstrated SAW interferometer
Observation of the interferogram of the acoustic interferometric process

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer includes technical conditions of the optomechanical interaction: red-detuned drive (Δ = ωm) giving a beam-splitter form, resolved-sideband limit (ωm ≫ κo), and pump enhancement of the single-photon coupling by intra-cavity photon number.
examples: The beam-splitter interaction requires red-detuned drive and resolved-sideband operation
Single-photon coupling gom is enhanced by intra-cavity photon number nc

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer cites concrete improvement routes: niobium electrodes, lithium niobate piezoelectric material, surface passivation, reduced filtering loss, better thermal contact, and target efficiencies (ηt ≈ 0.1, nadd ≲ 0.1).
examples: Lithium niobate offers larger piezoelectric coupling and energy participation
Eliminating filter insertion loss increases external efficiency by nearly two orders of magnitude
Niobium electrodes shorten quasiparticle lifetimes, improving repetition rate

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that current low photon flux prevents direct verification of quantum statistics (e.g., anti-bunching) of the emitted optical field, which improved devices would enable.
examples: Low photon flux does not allow direct verification of quantum statistics in the emitted light
Improved flux would enable observation of anti-bunching from transduced photons

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer clearly identifies at least two distinct studyable aspects of the coupled system: quantum transduction and delayed-choice quantum erasure.
examples: Two aspects: qubit-to-optical-photon transduction and quantum erasure with acoustic phonons
The hybrid system supports both transduction experiments and quantum eraser demonstrations
